_: Golden for the es.2_0td preset — D2 §9 1 and 12, D9 §3. The claim is about a breaker, not a fee: item 1 of the precedence, INV-1.

sources.periods: BOE-A-2020-1066 (CNMC Circular 3/2020) art. 7.3–7.4 as amended by Circular 1/2025, read 2026-09-23: 2.0TD's power term uses two periods — punta-llano (P1 + P2 of the energy periods, 08–24 on working weekdays) and valle (00–08, plus all hours of Saturdays, Sundays, 6 January and national holidays). That is `holidays: exclude` on the P1 filter, so a holiday falls through to P2 (D2 §2).
sources.limits: Not a fact about anyone: the template leaves the contracted kW to the household (D2 §6); this golden fills the flow's starting values.
sources.tolerance: None assumed (D-0521): the BOE text sets no interruptor tolerance, so the limit is the contract itself — the safe direction.
sources.no_peak: HLD §8's ES row: peak component `NoPeak`, hard limit `ContractedPower({P1, P2}, trip)`. Spain bills potencia contratada per day, not a measured peak, so there is no capacity metric and no ceiling — the breaker is the whole constraint.
sources.windows_priced: 0: nothing is priced on a version with no peak, though the windows are still recorded (INV-11).

limits.why: a working weekday before 08:00 is still P2
P1 starts at 08:00 local — the flip D2 §9 12 asks for
Reyes is a national holiday, so P2 (D2 §2, holidays: exclude on P1)

fill._: The flow's starting values (flow/steps.py LIMIT_DEFAULTS, D2 §6), filled into the template as the limits step would: 230 V x 20 A and x 25 A. A household's own contract replaces them.
